citations.claim: step 39 barely above wall, distance +0.0075 about to penetrate

counterfactual.change: Reduced bodies[0].vx from 46.59 to 10.0 (single field) keeping dt, steps, wall and other params identical; lower horizontal speed eliminates grazing penetration, scenario now passes with no violations.

explanation: Body 0 approaches thin horizontal wall (w=6.8,h=0.2 at y=8.6, top at 8.8) at very high horizontal speed ~46.6 m/s with dt=0.00394. At step 38 body is 0.087 above wall top (y=9.387), step 39 barely clears by 0.0075 (y=9.307), then at step 40 penetrates by 0.072 (y=9.228) and at step 41 penetration grows to 0.152 exceeding 0.15 limit (y=9.148). Substeps per step stay at 7, insufficient to prevent progressive interpenetration for fast grazing motion along the top face. Collision/positional correction fails to repel the body, so penetration accumulates each substep. Lowering horizontal speed removes the failure.
vision_note: The red circle travels horizontally just above the thin grey wall, starting with a small gap at step 38 and contacting the top edge at step 39. At steps 40 and 41 it visibly sinks into the wall with increasing overlap, appearing to intersect rather than rest on the surface.
